newsitem.title: THAILAND: Junior partner threatens to leave Thai coalition.
newsitem.headline: Junior partner threatens to leave Thai coalition.

text.p: A partner in outgoing Prime Minister Banharn Silpa-archa's outgoing ruling coalition on Thursday threatened to leave the government if a new premier was not named soon.
The Nam Thai party led by Deputy Prime Minister Amnuay Viravan, a junior but key member of the six-party coalition, made the threat as Banharn remained tight-lipped about his replacement.
Amnuay is seen by some analysts as a possible compromise choice for the premiership.

"The party is willing to cooperate with the ruling coalition in forming a new administration. But if there are troubles in forming the administration and it is unable to create public faith and acceptance, the party is ready review its position," Nam Thai said in a statement.
"So the Nam Thai party demands that the coalition partners speed up selection of a new prime minister and cabinet as soon as possible in order to regain the public faith and confidence."

Nam Thai only controls 18 of the 209 coalition seats but its leader, former banker Amnuay, is in demand because he is seen as the most qualified person to handle economic matters for any new administration, analysts said.

Banharn, who promised last weekend to quit by Saturday, has continued to keep the nation in the dark about who would replace him. Coalition partners have huddled in groups trying to arrive at a compromise successor.

Coalition sources said the front-runner was Defence Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh, who leads the New Aspiration Party, the second largest in the coalition with 57 seats. But he lacks solid support from Banharn's Chart Thai party, which controls 91 seats.

Chavalit is seen as the one who, along with other coalition allies, engineered Banharn's downfall by forcing the prime minister to announce his resignation in return for support at a parliamentary no-confidence vote against him last Saturday.

Other possible replacements were Chart Thai party elder Pramarn Adireksarn or the leader of the opposition Chart Pattana party and former premier Chatichai Choonhavan, who controls 53 of the 391 seats in parliament, politicians and analysts said.
